segments.source: Today, thanks to deep learning algorithms of artificial intelligence, we have the possibility to automate the classification of images, so this tool can help medical personnel in the classification and early detection of breast cancer. In this way, women suffering from this disease could be diagnosed automatically, in time to start treatment.
segments.en: Deep learning makes it possible to explore automated medical-image classification. WomanLife investigates this with breast ultrasound images as an educational prototype, with the longer-term aim of studying tools that could support healthcare professionals.
segments.es: El aprendizaje profundo permite explorar la clasificación automatizada de imágenes médicas. En WomanLife investigamos esta posibilidad con ecografías de mama, como un prototipo educativo orientado a estudiar posibles herramientas de apoyo al personal sanitario.

editorialReview.scope: Spanish and English wording

segments.source: Breast cancer is the most common type of cancer in women and is also one of the main causes of death according to the WHO (WHO, 2020). Early detection is the single most important factor in lowering cancer treatment costs and mortality. To make it possible it is necessary to have medical ultrasound images and specialists who can explain them. However, the lack of these creates a gap in access to early treatment in countries with little or not enough access to specialized diagnostic services and whose population receives low and middle income.
segments.en: Breast cancer is a major health concern, and timely detection and treatment can improve outcomes. Unequal access to examinations and specialists motivated us to explore supporting tools, without replacing clinical assessment.
segments.es: El cáncer de mama es un problema de salud relevante, y la detección y el tratamiento oportunos pueden mejorar los resultados. El acceso desigual a pruebas y especialistas motivó nuestro interés por estudiar herramientas de apoyo, sin sustituir la evaluación clínica.

editorialReview.scope: Spanish and English wording

segments.source: Our project consists of the detection and classification of breast cancer in women between 25 and 75 years old. This is possible from the development of an deep learning model trained with images obtained using ultrasound scanners that result in the segmentation of the type of cancer that could be suffered.
segments.en: The project classifies ultrasound images from a dataset collected from women aged 25–75. The model estimates one of three image categories; it does not segment lesions or independently establish a person’s diagnosis.
segments.es: El proyecto clasifica imágenes ecográficas de un dataset obtenido de mujeres de entre 25 y 75 años. El modelo estima una de tres categorías de imagen; no segmenta lesiones ni determina por sí solo el diagnóstico de una persona.

editorialReview.scope: Spanish and English wording

segments.source: Allow women suffering from breast cancer to be automatically diagnosed using a deep learning model so that they can start treatment early and safely, reducing costs and the mortality rate. To meet this objective, we have proposed a tool that uses artificial intelligence to provide greater agility to the process through self-diagnosis with ultrasound images.
segments.en: Explore an ultrasound-image classifier that, after appropriate clinical validation, could be studied as a support tool for healthcare professionals. The prototype is not intended for self-diagnosis and does not demonstrate reduced costs or mortality.
segments.es: Explorar un modelo de clasificación de ecografías que, tras una eventual validación clínica, pudiera estudiarse como apoyo al personal sanitario. El prototipo presentado no está destinado al autodiagnóstico ni demuestra reducción de costes o mortalidad.

segments.source: WomanLife is intended to be an easy-to-access, low-cost medical diagnostic tool.
segments.en: WomanLife explores a possible tool to support ultrasound-image analysis.
segments.es: WomanLife explora una posible herramienta de apoyo al análisis de ecografías.

editorialReview.scope: Spanish and English wording

segments.source: This AI is not only beneficial for women who use it but also has the potential to become a medical assistant. We want to clarify that WomanLife does not intend to replace medical specialists but to provide a tool that facilitates their work.
segments.en: The ambition is to support specialists, but further testing is needed to determine whether the model has clinical value. The educational application does not replace medical consultation.
segments.es: La aspiración es facilitar el trabajo de especialistas, pero hacen falta pruebas adicionales para determinar si el modelo aporta utilidad clínica. La aplicación educativa no sustituye la consulta médica.

segments.source: Our project also developed an application that, given an image scanned with the camera or selected from the gallery, goes through the developed network and returns a series of probabilities related to the type of cancer suffered.
segments.en: We also built an application that accepts an image from the camera or gallery and returns model scores for the dataset’s three classes. Those scores are neither a diagnosis nor validated clinical probabilities of having cancer.
segments.es: También desarrollamos una aplicación que recibe una imagen de la cámara o la galería y devuelve las puntuaciones del modelo para las tres clases del dataset. Esas puntuaciones no son un diagnóstico ni una probabilidad clínica validada de padecer cáncer.
